prompts.pond-kinds-signs:
Use case: AI-illustrated hobby guide that helps a beginner garden-pond keeper recognise what is wrong with their pond fish.
LOOK: every cell is a natural, clear, believable photo of pond fish, taken one of two ordinary ways that pond keepers really use: (a) LOOKING DOWN INTO A CLEAR GARDEN POND from the edge: slightly green-tinted but clear water, stones, a few lily pads or plants at the edges, daylight; or (b) a fish lifted into a shallow round floating INSPECTION BOWL (a plain pale blue or white plastic bowl of pond water) so it can be looked at closely from above or the side. The named fish is the clear subject: large in the frame, fully in view, NOT hidden under plants, NOT cut off by the cell edge. Clear water, no thick algae soup, no heavy reflections hiding the fish. Not studio-perfect either: an everyday hobbyist photo with natural colours. Show the problem the way it typically really looks on a pond fish (how big, how many, where on the body), NOT one tiny perfect mark on an otherwise perfect fish. The problem must be easy to see at thumbnail size. Photographic and believable. Not cartoons, icons, illustrations, diagrams, 3D renders or typography. No people, faces or hands unless the cell names them. Absolutely no text, letters, numbers, labels, logos, watermarks, arrows or symbols anywhere in the image.
STRICT CONTACT SHEET for cropping into twelve separate pictures: exactly FOUR equal-width columns and THREE equal-height rows, twelve equal square cells covering the complete image edge to edge. No gutters, no borders, no outer margin. Every cell is its own separate photo with its own background. Nothing crosses a cell boundary; keep the main subject inside the central 85 percent of its cell. Never put a cell's subject into another cell. Follow the exact row-major order below.
Fish (draw each one exactly as named): KOI = an ornamental Japanese carp, long torpedo body with barbels on its lip; KOHAKU = a white koi with red patches; SHOWA or SANKE = white, red and black koi; OGON = plain metallic gold or platinum koi. POND GOLDFISH = a slim single-tailed COMET or SHUBUNKIN (not a fancy round goldfish unless named): orange, red-and-white or calico. GOLDEN ORFE = a slim orange-gold fish with a pointed head, swimming in shoals near the surface. Sizes: koi 30-60 cm, goldfish 10-20 cm, orfe 20-30 cm.
Row 1 column 1: HEALTHY KOI seen from above in a clear garden pond: a KOHAKU, a SHOWA and a gold OGON swimming together, bright and clean.
Row 1 column 2: HEALTHY POND GOLDFISH seen from above in a clear garden pond: a few orange COMETS and a calico SHUBUNKIN swimming among lily pads.
Row 1 column 3: HEALTHY OTHER POND FISH seen from above in a clear garden pond: a shoal of slim orange-gold GOLDEN ORFE near the surface and a dark green tench lower down.
Row 1 column 4: ANCHOR WORM: a KOHAKU koi in a pale blue inspection bowl, seen from the side and above, with three thin whitish-green THREAD-LIKE WORMS about 1 cm long sticking straight out of its skin, each with a small RED INFLAMED SPOT where it is buried and two tiny egg sacs on the free end.
Row 2 column 1: FISH LICE: a gold OGON koi in a white inspection bowl seen from above, with four flat, round, see-through greenish-brown DISC-SHAPED LICE about 5-8 mm wide clinging flat to its back and near its fins, small red marks around them.
Row 2 column 2: ULCER: a KOHAKU koi in a pale blue inspection bowl, side view, with one clear OPEN ROUND SORE about the size of a coin on its flank: a red crater with missing scales and a white rim.
Row 2 column 3: RED STREAKS: an orange COMET goldfish in a white inspection bowl, side view, with bright RED BLOOD STREAKS in its tail and fins and a blotchy red flush on its belly.
Row 2 column 4: WHITE SPOT: a SHOWA koi in a white inspection bowl seen from above, its body and fins sprinkled with many small raised WHITE DOTS like grains of salt.
Row 3 column 1: COTTON-WOOL FUNGUS: an orange COMET goldfish in a pale blue inspection bowl, side view, with a fluffy WHITE-GREY COTTON-WOOL TUFT growing on its side and another on its tail.
Row 3 column 2: SCALES STICKING OUT: a red-and-white COMET goldfish in a white inspection bowl, seen from above at an angle, its body swollen and its scales RAISED AND STICKING OUT like an open pine cone.
Row 3 column 3: FLASHING: in a clear garden pond seen from above, a KOHAKU koi twisted on its side, RUBBING and scraping its flank against a stone on the bottom, a little swirl of disturbed silt; other koi nearby.
Row 3 column 4: GASPING AT THE SURFACE: a garden pond seen from above where several KOI and goldfish crowd at the surface with their MOUTHS OPEN ABOVE THE WATER, gulping air, ripples around their mouths, on a hot still day.

Row 1 column 1: SITTING ON THE BOTTOM: a clear, cold garden pond seen from above in late autumn, a few brown leaves floating, several KOI resting still and close together on the bottom with their fins folded.

Row 3 column 1: ULCER DISEASE: a SHOWA koi in a pale blue inspection bowl seen from above, with a deep RED ULCER on its back with a white edge and a second smaller sore starting near its tail.
Row 3 column 2: BACTERIAL INFECTION: an orange-and-white COMET goldfish in a white inspection bowl, side view, with RED BLOTCHES on its body, red streaks in its fins and a frayed, reddened tail.
Row 3 column 3: SKIN FLUKES: a KOHAKU koi in a white inspection bowl, side view, its skin covered in a dull GREY-WHITE MUCUS HAZE, fins clamped, one gill cover held open slightly; looks dull compared with a normal glossy koi.
Row 3 column 4: WHITE SPOT IN A POND: a few orange COMETS and a SHUBUNKIN seen from above in a pale blue inspection bowl, all covered in small raised WHITE DOTS on their bodies and fins.
